title: MeridianBank POC scoping - workload modeling
summary: POC scoping focused on workload characterization and benchmarking for MeridianBank's new chat-assistant. Discussed QPS/concurrency, token distributions, latency SLOs, security requirements and a 4-week POC plan with benchmarks and handoff steps.
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-07 10:00 AM PT
Duration: 52 minutes
Recording: internal link (shared)
Attendees: Priya Shah (Redwood AE), Daniel Ortega (Redwood SE), Laura Kim (Meridian - Dir ML), Samir Patel (Meridian - Platform), Ellen Torres (Meridian - Security), Tom Reynolds (Meridian PM)

[00:00] Priya Shah: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intro — i'm priya, ae on the account, daniel is our se. can we do quick round robin?
[00:12] Laura Kim: hi laura here, director of ml, i'll be owning success criteria and evals.
[00:18] Samir Patel: samir, platform engineering, i'll help with infra and networking.
[00:23] Ellen Torres: ellen, security/compliance. we have SOC2 compliance requirements and KMS for encryption.
[00:28] Tom Reynolds: tom product manager, timeline oriented.
[00:33] Daniel Ortega: cool thanks. goal for today: nail down workload profile for the POC so we can size dedicated vs hosted, and agree on benchmarks and timeline.

[01:05] Priya Shah: Laura earlier mentioned a chat assistant for customer support and internal ops. can you share rough traffic numbers, qps, expected peaks?
[01:14] Laura Kim: sure. right now baseline bot traffic is small but for launch we expect about 40 qps average during peak hours, with concurrency around 15-25 active sessions. bursty patterns — marketing promos could spike to 180-200 qps for 2-3 minutes.
[01:35] Daniel Ortega: good, that helps. what's the typical prompt size? average input tokens and expected model output length?
[01:42] Laura Kim: inputs average 60-90 tokens; some long ones 300+ (account summaries). outputs usually 120-200 tokens, but in structured replies sometimes up to 400. overall median output ~150.
[01:58] Samir Patel: we have latency goals: p95 < 350ms for simple queries, p95 < 800ms for longer context ones. cost is a factor — want to keep monthly inference cost under $12k for first phase.
[02:16] Priya Shah: helpful. success criteria we typically see: correctness/quality gates (human eval on representative prompts), latency SLOs, throughput at target qps with less than X percent error, and ops integration (SSO, audit logs). Laura, would you add acceptance thresholds?
[02:32] Laura Kim: yes, quality: BLEU-like metrics aren't great for chat but we'll use sample eval set and human rating — 90% rated acceptable. Latency: p95 < 350ms for short prompts, p50 < 150ms. Reliability: 99.5% of requests served without fallback.

[03:05] Daniel Ortega: ok for modeling we need a distribution: 70% of requests are short (<=100 input tokens), 25% medium (100-300), 5% long (>300). outputs: 60% under 150 tokens, 30% 150-300, 10% >300. we'll simulate spikes to 200 qps with 50% short requests.
[03:30] Tom Reynolds: is that with context caching? we rely on session context for churn reduction.
[03:35] Daniel Ortega: yes we assume prefix caching for repeated flows; but account-summary calls won't cache well. we'll parameterize cache-hit rate (expected ~35%).

[04:02] Priya Shah: on model choices — are you leaning hosted vs dedicated vs private?
[04:09] Samir Patel: initial preference is hosted for speed, but we need VPC/private for production by month 3 due to data residency and audit requirements. so the POC should validate routing and performance on both hosted and a dedicated reserved pool.
[04:27] Ellen Torres: security is important — SOC2 certificate required, SAML SSO for console, KMS integration, and audit logs retention for 1 year.

[05:00] Daniel Ortega: for benchmarks we'll run: 1) baseline latency bench at 50 qps sustained for 30 minutes with realistic token distributions; 2) burst test to 200 qps for 5 minutes; 3) end-to-end degradation tests with KV cache cold start; 4) cost projection run using sampled token profile for 1M requests.
[05:25] Laura Kim: that sounds good — need to see per-model p95 and p99 numbers, plus token-level cost.
[05:34] Daniel Ortega: we'll provide a benchmark spreadsheet with: qps, concurrency, avg input/output tokens, latency p50/p95/p99, cost per 1M tokens, and recommended quantization/instance type.

[06:00] Priya Shah: timeline — we usually do a 4-week POC: week 0 (kickoff + infra setup), week 1 (initial benchmarks on hosted), week 2 (integration + targeted model tuning), week 3 (dedicated capacity tests + security reqs), week 4 (wrap up, final benchmark, exec review). is that acceptable?
[06:20] Tom Reynolds: yes 4 weeks is fine but we need to align with our compliance team; can you support a private deployment test in week 3 if we give credentials?
[06:29] Daniel Ortega: yes we can run a private dedicated test if network peering/VPN is available; will need firewall rules and an SSH bastion or a peering config.

[07:00] Ellen Torres: about data retention and KMS — we need to know whether tokens are stored, where logs live, and how key rotation works.
[07:08] Priya Shah: Redwood stores logs in encrypted S3 in the customer's region for private deployments — for hosted we can provide an option to disable storing request/content, and send audit logs to your syslog. we'll share our security deck and SOC2 report.
[07:26] Ellen Torres: ok please send SOC2 and our legal may ask for HIPAA addendum later.

[07:45] Samir Patel: questions about routing fallback — if dedicated capacity is saturated, can requests route to hosted with redaction?
[07:54] Daniel Ortega: yes there's smart routing: you can set policy to failover to hosted model variant; we can redact PII at the edge or run a redaction lambda before sending. performance and cost implications documented in the handbook.

[08:20] Laura Kim: for success criteria, we also want an automated regression check — if new model increases latency or drops quality on eval set, block rollout. can Redwood do that?
[08:30] Daniel Ortega: yes Redwood Optimize supports automated eval checkpoints and alerts. we'll wire up your eval set and run nightly checks during POC.

[09:00] Priya Shah: next, the metrics you want in the benchmark report — token counts, per-route latency, cache-hit rate, and cost. any additions?
[09:10] Samir Patel: please include memory/KV cache warmup times and tail latency (p99.9) during cold starts.

[09:28] Tom Reynolds: ok on deliverables — can we distill a short acceptance checklist?
[09:34] Laura Kim: yes: 1) p95 short queries <350ms on dedicated; 2) can handle sustained 50 qps and 2-minute bursts to 180 qps; 3) quality threshold 90% on eval set; 4) security checklists satisfied (SOC2, KMS, SSO); 5) documented cost projections under target budget.

[10:05] Daniel Ortega: great. any blockers from your side for starting next monday?
[10:10] Samir Patel: we need an estimated infra footprint and credentials for peering, plus a small data sample for evals. we'll get that by friday.
[10:18] Priya Shah: we'll prepare an engagement doc, benchmark plan, and a model/instance recommendation. we'll share the security pack and schedule the kickoff.

[10:35] Priya Shah: recap of next steps and owners — i'll summarize in the follow-up. thanks everyone.
[11:00] (call ends)
next_steps: Priya to share engagement doc + benchmark spreadsheet (due 2026-11-10)
Meridian to provide eval sample & peering details (due 2026-11-12)
SE to schedule kickoff and private peering test (target start 2026-11-15)
action_items: Priya Shah - send engagement doc, benchmark plan, security pack - 2026-11-10
Samir Patel - provide network peering details and sample eval set - 2026-11-12
Daniel Ortega - prepare benchmark harness and run initial hosted baseline - 2026-11-16
Ellen Torres - review SOC2 docs and confirm any additional compliance asks - 2026-11-13
